note: Analyst reading of the news, written from logged events. Not data. The weekly agent replaces it every week.
headline: The Saudi-led coalition stepped up air strikes in Yemen: it says it hit 60 Houthi military targets on Nov 17 (#1376) and Hodeidah port facilities and Houthi missile and drone sites in Sanaa on Nov 20 (#1377). Al Jazeera's reporter calls the Nov 20 strikes the heaviest since the conflict began.

Houthi-side authorities report people killed and hurt: six injured at a Sanaa fuel station (Nov 22, #1379), four killed and 18 wounded at a Hodeidah telecom building (Nov 23, #1380) and 19 killed on a civilian boat (Nov 20, #1381). These are claims; the coalition had not commented and none is confirmed.

A Houthi drone aimed at Riyadh was destroyed and a ballistic missile aimed at the western region was intercepted on Nov 22; no casualties or damage were reported (#1378). The Houthi threat to Saudi airspace and Red Sea ports from Nov 20 is still open (#1375).

No US move against the Houthis was found: no strike, sanctions, naval action or talks, and the coverage read names no US role in the Saudi strikes. Reuters' sources said on Nov 19 that Trump has not agreed to US strikes and the US gives intelligence and targeting help (#1372).
pending: Whether the US joins the Saudi strikes (#1341, #1372); no decision found by Nov 23
